web.title: Websites
web.intro: Galleries and pattern collections for marketing sites, landing pages, portfolios, stores and their sections. Galleries show what designers admire, not what converts or what users can use: pair one gallery with a real-product or evidence source.
sections: For overall art direction. Open the live site - thumbnails hide type rendering, motion and responsiveness.
For page narrative and section order. Full-page captures show how the argument is sequenced.
When the question is one section (hero, nav, pricing, footer, CTA, email). Compare ten solutions to the same problem.
Dark mode, brutalist, e-commerce, portfolios, and Japanese galleries - the best public references for CJK typographic layout.
Ambition, motion and WebGL. Juries reward spectacle; usability and conversion are not judged.
Structure and messaging evidence for pages that must persuade.

app-ui.title: Product UI
app-ui.intro: What actually ships: screens and flows from real products, component references, official platform guidelines, published design systems, data visualisation and AI product patterns. Prefer these over concept shots for anything users will operate daily.
sections: Look up the screen type or flow in several shipped products before designing it. Convention is a feature.
Anatomy, naming, states and keyboard behaviour of a component across systems.
Authoritative and versioned. Check the current page before relying on a remembered number.
Read the pattern and content guidance, not just the components. Pick a system from a comparable domain.
Choose the chart from the question being asked; study dashboard genres before laying one out.
Patterns for chat, copilots and agents. This field moves quickly: date what you take.
Game HUDs, fictional interfaces and small delights - for immersive, full-screen and one-memorable-moment problems.

motion.title: Motion
motion.intro: Recordings of motion in shipped products are the best teacher: watch them slowed down and note duration, easing, origin and what does not move. Then tools to author curves and springs, official guidelines, and the few writers worth reading.
sections: Start here for any in-product animation.
Web motion showcases and asset libraries
Expressive and experimental work, usually with source. Check licences on assets.
Author curves and springs by eye, then record the numbers as tokens.
Token tables, principles, and the rules for motion sensitivity.
Writing and courses on motion craft
A small set that repays reading in full.
API references and example collections for SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter.

icons.title: Icons
icons.intro: Pick one family per product and record its licence. Raw-SVG endpoints are listed so an agent can pull an icon without installing a package.
sections: Choose by style fit, coverage, weights, platform packages, licence and maintenance.
For finding a concept across sets. Do not mix the results in one interface.
Trademarks remain with their owners; follow each brand's usage rules.
Read one before drawing a custom icon or writing the rules for a set.
Galleries for the idiom, tools for the packaging. Platform specs are perishable.
Optimise, edit paths numerically, convert, trace.

assets.title: Visual assets
assets.intro: Illustrations, 3D, photography, mock-ups, and code-native backgrounds. Licence mistakes are the main risk in this domain: the Access column states the licence reality for each source.
sections: One style per product. Widely used free sets are instantly recognisable; restyle or use sparingly.
Models, materials and scenes. Check the runtime cost before embedding.
Treat images consistently. Never use unlicensed images found online.
Clean frames usually present UI better than staged scenes.
Often better recreated in code for control. Interpolate gradients perceptually and add grain against banding.

brand.title: Brand identity
brand.intro: Archives to see how a form has already been solved, publications that critique identity work, real guideline documents, studio case studies, and the tools for naming and trademark checks.
sections: Search the client's initial, shape family and industry before sketching. Similarity to an existing mark is a legal risk, not only a taste issue.
Learn the vocabulary of identity critique and how systems extend beyond the logo.
Open three guidelines from a similar industry and compare their contents before writing one.
Read how the problem is framed and how the work is presented in application.
An agent cannot clear a mark. These tools find obvious conflicts; a professional search is still required.

graphic.title: Graphic design
graphic.intro: Posters, archives, decks, covers, packaging and the publications that track contemporary graphic design. The strongest moves available to a code-based designer are typographic, so typographic posters and historical archives are the richest sources.
sections: Study grid, scale contrast and how little is on the page.
Authentic period references instead of pastiche.
Narrative order first, slide system second.
Single-idea composition under a fixed frame.
Sizes are perishable: verify with the platform before export.

type.title: Typography
type.intro: Open font sources with clear licences, commercial foundries worth knowing, type seen in real use, tools, the guides that matter, and a full section for Chinese type and typesetting.
sections: The route away from default typefaces without licence risk. Self-host; do not hot-link.
Trial and free-to-try files are for mock-ups only and must not ship.
See a typeface set in real context before choosing it.
Scales, fluid type, system stacks, inspection, metrics and subsetting.
Read the first two in full once.
Open-licence Chinese fonts, licence directories, web-font slicing, and the typesetting rules for punctuation and mixed scripts. Commercial Chinese font licensing is actively enforced.

color.title: Colour
color.intro: Palette inspiration, tools that build perceptually even and accessible scales, contrast and colour-vision checks, and the articles that explain why. Compute contrast; never estimate it.
sections: For mood and starting points. A palette is not a system until roles and contrast are defined.
Generate scales in a perceptual space; map steps to roles.
Contrast, colour vision and data palettes
WCAG 2 ratios are the legal baseline; APCA is informative draft guidance.
The reasoning behind modern UI colour systems and dark mode.

code.title: Code and open-source projects
code.intro: The agent's design medium is code. These are the projects to know: other AI design skills and bridges, component libraries and primitives by stack, animation and graphics libraries, token tooling, and the pipeline that turns HTML, SVG and markup into images, PDFs and slides. Verify APIs against the installed version.
sections: AI design skills, formats and agent tooling
Prior art for this suite, the DESIGN.md format, and the tools that give an agent eyes and access to design files.
Use the host project's library. When choosing, prefer accessible primitives and a real theme API.
Technique references. A page assembled from these looks like every other; use one signature moment and restyle it.
Match the tool to the job; check licences for commercial use.
One token source, built to every platform.
How code-made graphics become PNG, SVG, PDF and PPTX, and how fonts are subset.
Scriptable or open tools that complement a code-first workflow.
Breadth for discovery. Judge quality yourself.

reading.title: Reading
reading.intro: The articles, books, courses and guidelines whose ideas shape this suite. Prefer primary, durable sources; name the principle when justifying a decision.
sections: The details that make interfaces feel right, and robust CSS thinking.
Why models produce generic design and what changes that; design in AI-era products.
Hierarchy, spacing, perception. Start with the first three.
Evidence to cite instead of opinion.
Briefs, critique formats, and explaining decisions to stakeholders.
Worth their price for building real skill.
Domestic case studies and team blogs for Chinese-market context.

general.title: Communities, moodboards and feeds
general.intro: Cross-discipline sources for scanning and collecting. High volume, mixed signal: concept shots ignore real content, states and accessibility. Use for visual treatment and trend awareness, then verify against real products.
sections: Read case-study process, not just covers.
Collect from outside the interface-design bubble.
Trend radar. Date what you take; fashion expires.
Domestic portfolios, moodboards and shared design files.
